text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
FromCS(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
HasPartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakesDatabase(x) ::: x takes the database course.
InstructedByDavid(x) ::: x is instructed by professor David.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.

Premises:
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x)) → ¬FromCS(x)) ::: No students who work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ HasPartTimeJob(x)) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All students who have part-time jobs offered by the university are students who work in the library.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ TakesDatabase(x)) → FromCS(x)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ InstructedByDavid(x)) → TakesDatabase(x)) ::: All students instructed by professor David are taking the database course.
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ WorksInLab(x)) → InstructedByDavid(x)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by professor David.
Student(james) ∧ WorksInLab(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬HasPartTimeJob(jack) ∧ ¬WorksInLab(jack) ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.

Conclusion:
TakesDatabase(james) ⊕ HasPartTimeJob(james) ::: James either takes the database course or has a part-time job offered by the university.
